messages:
andrew: quick heads-up — synthetic blackbox checks in ap-southeast-1 are showing TLS handshake spikes and intermittent 502s for /v1/stream endpoints since ~01:20 UTC. p95 jumped to ~820ms repeatedly. anyone seeing this elsewhere?

katie: seeing same in ap-south1 but lower freq. looks correlated with our streaming synthetic job schedule (every 20s). :thinking_face:

sre-bot: ALERT: blackbox_tls_handshake_failures{region=\"ap-southeast-1\"} > 0 for 3m — fired at 2025-11-07T01:23:10Z

oliver: could be SNAT port exhaustion on the probe hosts or upstream LB spinning new handshakes under load. can we get conn state dumps from one of the failing pods?

andrew: grabbing a netstat now from probe-pod-7:```
netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
# 17890
```

liya: 17k TIME_WAITs is suspicious — probs hitting ephemeral port pool. are we reusing keepalives? blackbox probe uses short-lived conns by default.

katie: yes, probe job uses curl per request (no keepalive). solution options: enable HTTP/1.1 persistent connections for streaming checks, or rotate source IPs / add more NAT IPs.

oliver: also saw this in Prom: `node_netstat_TimeWait` trending up on the probe fleet. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/s/d-synthetic/blackbox-checks — look at instance=probe-runner-*

andrew: re: alerts — current firing threshold is any nonzero TLS failures for 1m. that's too chatty when we have ephemeral port pressure. propose: change alert to `rate(blackbox_tls_handshake_failures[5m]) > 0 and increase for: 5m` and only page on >5% of instances.

liya: agreed. also consider sampling: run full-frequency checks only for regions that host traffic or have high SLO impact. reduce non-critical regions to 1/6th frequency. that will cut synthetic egress by ~80% for low-traffic regions.

katie: +1. cost note: synthetic checks contribute noticeable egress and GPU infer cost when we run full model stubs. we can switch low-fidelity checks to header-only or /health endpoints to keep coverage but reduce compute.

andrew: quick config snippet to enable persistent conn in the probe job (suggested):```
- name: blackbox-http
  params:
    http:
      persistent: true
      keepalive_timeout: 60
```

oliver: if we switch to persistent we should still randomize source ports to avoid long TIME_WAIT accumulation. also increase kernel ephemeral port range on probe nodes: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=10000 65535` and lower TIME_WAIT reuse timeout.

liya: another idea: stagger the probe schedule with jitter so not all runners hammer at exact second boundaries — small change but big impact on spikes.

andrew: agreed. action items: 1) change alert rule to 5m window + >5% instance impact (katie) 2) pilot persistent conn + jitter on 10% of probe fleet (oliver) 3) increase ephemeral port range on probe nodes (liya) 4) switch low-impact regions to header-only checks (andrew) — target deploy in 24h.

katie: i'll update the alert in prometheus and add a documented rationale in the grafana alert notes.

oliver: will ship pilot recipe and run a 6h soak, will post netstat+prom screenshots in this thread.

liya: i'll coordinate kernel sysctl rollout with infra and add a preflight check for TIME_WAIT thresholds.

andrew: thanks team. if pilot looks good we can reduce synthetic frequency and reclaim ~0.12 vGPU per 1000 synthetic requests which helps cost. we'll revisit next week after soak. :thumbsup:
